Question 1
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=2e2t, where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=e2 and velocity v=e2 when t=1, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=2e2t+e2
b
x(t)=2e2t+te2+12e2
c
x(t)=e2t+te2
d
x(t)=12e2t+12e2
e
x(t)=12e2t+te2+e2
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=e^{2t}+C. Since v(1)=e^2, C=0. Integrating again gives x(t)=\frac12 e^{2t}+D. Since x(1)=e^2, D=\frac12 e^2, so option d satisfies both initial conditions.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2{e}^{2t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x={e}^{2}$ and velocity $v={e}^{2}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
after.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2{e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & ={e}^{2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & ={e}^{2(1)}+C \\ {e}^{2} & ={e}^{2}+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)={e}^{2t}.$ 

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2(1)}+K \\ {e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+K \\ K & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.
$$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=2e2t, where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=e2 and velocity v=e2 when t=1, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=2e2t+e2
b
x(t)=2e2t+te2+12e2
c
x(t)=e2t+te2
d
x(t)=12e2t+12e2
e
x(t)=12e2t+te2+e2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity v(t):

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫2e2tdt=e2t+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=e2. Substituting this into the above gives

e2=e2(1)+Ce2=e2+CC=0.

So the velocity is given by v(t)=e2t.

Now, we integrate the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫e2tdt=12e2t+K

To determine K, we use the fact that x(1)=e2. Substituting this into the above gives

e2=12e2(1)+Ke2=12e2+KK=12e2.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=12e2t+12e2.

content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2{e}^{2t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x={e}^{2}$ and velocity $v={e}^{2}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
content.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2{e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & ={e}^{2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & ={e}^{2(1)}+C \\ {e}^{2} & ={e}^{2}+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)={e}^{2t}.$ 

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2(1)}+K \\ {e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+K \\ K & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.
$$

b

d

x(t)=2sin⁡(t)+2t

decision.explanation: Integrating gives v(t)=2sin(t)+C. The condition v(π/2)=4 gives C=2. Thus x(t)=-2cos(t)+2t+K. Using x(π/2)=2π gives K=π, so option c is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=2\pi $ and velocity $v=4$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\text{d}t \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(\frac{\pi }{2})=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+C \\ 4 & =2(1)+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+2.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+2)\text{d}t \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(\frac{\pi }{2})=2\pi .$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+2(\frac{\pi }{2})+K \\ 2\pi  & =-2(0)+\pi +K \\ K & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2t+\pi .
$$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=2cos⁡(t), where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=2π and velocity v=4 when t=π2, calculate the position x of the particle at time t.

a
x(t)=2cos⁡(t)−2t+3π
b
x(t)=−2sin⁡(t)+2t+π
c
x(t)=−2cos⁡(t)+2t+π
d
x(t)=−2cos⁡(t)+4t
e
x(t)=2sin⁡(t)+2t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity v(t):

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫2cos⁡(t)dt=2sin⁡(t)+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(π2)=4. Substituting this into the above gives

4=2sin⁡(π2)+C4=2(1)+CC=2.

So the velocity is given by v(t)=2sin⁡(t)+2.

Now, we integrate the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(2sin⁡(t)+2)dt=−2cos⁡(t)+2t+K

To determine K, we use the fact that x(π2)=2π. Substituting this into the above gives

2π=−2cos⁡(π2)+2(π2)+K2π=−2(0)+π+KK=π.

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+C \\ 4 & =2(1)+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+2)\text{d}t \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2t+K\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+2(\frac{\pi }{2})+K \\ 2\pi  & =-2(0)+\pi +K \\ K & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x(t)=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2t+\pi .
